chunks: Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
“If a free man kills a slave, he is made to pay his value and is disciplined.”
It was said: “Even if his value were twenty thousand dirhams?” He said: “The value of the slave does not exceed the blood-money of free persons.”

key_terms.الْحُرُّ: a free person, in contrast to a slave
key_terms.الْعَبْدَ: the slave who is killed in this ruling
key_terms.دِيَةَ الْأَحْرَارِ: the blood-money legally fixed for free persons
key_terms.عِشْرِينَ أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ: twenty thousand dirhams, given as an example of a high valuation
key_terms.غُرِّمَ: he is held financially liable to pay compensation
key_terms.قِيمَتَهُ: his market value, meaning the slave’s assessed monetary worth

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a free man kills a slave in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding a free man who kills a slave: he must pay the slave’s value and be disciplined. It also sets a legal limit that the slave’s assessed value, for compensation purposes, does not exceed the diyah of free persons.
